## 5. Tokenizer and training tokens (real Qwen2.5 tokenizer)

- Digits: every 4-digit number tokenizes to 4 single-digit tokens (27000 contexts checked: bare, 'Is n a prime number?', 'Is n divisible by 7?'); 6-digit examples also split into single digits.
- Loss-bearing tokens per 180-example draw (completion + EOS, one epoch; x3 for the 3 epochs), mean over seeds 0-2:

| task | A | B | C | Bprime | B / A | B tokens per whitespace token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| prime | 720 | 33575 | 32245 | - | 46.6 | 2.54 |
| div7 | 720 | 20250 | 20312 | 20430 | 28.1 | 1.88 |
| valid | 720 | 10099 | 10229 | - | 14.0 | 1.44 |
| div2 | 720 | 20250 | 20273 | - | 28.1 | 1.88 |
| div3 | 720 | 20250 | 20288 | - | 28.1 | 1.88 |
| div11 | 720 | 21409 | 21467 | - | 29.7 | 1.98 |
| div13 | 720 | 21525 | 21571 | - | 29.9 | 1.99 |
| div7_6d | 720 | 27450 | 27484 | - | 38.1 | 1.96 |

- Sampling replica check: the whitespace-token count of the replicated draw equals the train_tokens recorded by the worker in 17/17 recorded (task, arm, seed) cells; A, B and C of one seed train on the same 180 items (pools share item order). C's per-draw length differs slightly from B's because C's traces are permuted across the whole pool (length-matched corpus-wide, not per draw).

## Caveats

- Per-item predictions are recovered from correctness bitmaps (wrong = flipped label); an unparseable answer ('?') counts as a flip. Where results/v2/gens exist, rules.json uses the observed predictions instead.
- 'max on test' probe numbers are selected on the test set (optimistic); the CV-selected probe is the honest one.
- The engineered number features include digit sum mod 3 (= n mod 3) and alternating sum mod 11 (= n mod 11), so on div3/div11 the 'engineered' probes are handed the answer; the one-hot probes are the fair surface baseline there. On prime they supply partial-sieve features (n mod 2, 3, 5, 11), which is why they beat A.
- On prime_hard every item is odd with no factor <= 7, so 'last digit in {1,3,7,9}', 'odd' and 'no factor <= 7' all predict Yes on every item: any of them gives 50% there.
- The pooled Wilson interval treats items x seeds as independent; the paired bootstrap respects item pairing and seed variation, and is wide when only 2 seeds exist (e.g. valid B: 100% and 80%).
